problem: A customer service representative resolves a caller’s issue with a $45%$ chance during each minute of a call. The call continues until the issue is resolved. Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability that it will take exactly $5$ minutes to resolve the issue is{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of minutes until the representative resolves the issue. Since the chance of resolving the issue in any given minute is $45%,$ the number of minutes until the issue is resolved can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success

$$
p=45%=\frac{45}{100}=0.45.
$$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.45).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.45)^{x-1}(0.45) \\  & =(0.55)^{x-1}(0.45)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that the representative will resolve the issue for the first time in the $5$th minute is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=5) & =f(5) \\  & =(0.55)^{5-1}(0.45) \\  & =(0.55)^{4}(0.45) \\  & ≈0.041,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
